analysis: The two supplied units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1613-2014 and 2015-2406). The file_changes patch shows documentation-only edits at base line 453 and later regions (head 453-473, 3239-3242, 3255-3286). They add cluster onboarding stop semantics (`darkbloom cluster stop`, `stopsAsked` counter, `ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked`). None of the changed ranges fall inside the supplied units, and the units contain no changed lines. I found no security-relevant regression in the supplied text. I reviewed the content against the threat model: GLM admission and capacity, the prefix cache, encrypted SSD checkpoints (T-041), chunk batching and session binding on the coordinator-to-provider channel (T-008, T-010), calibration and posture gating, and audio rejection. All of it is pre-existing descriptive prose, not a new control, and nothing weakens a stated mitigation or invalidates a threat assumption. The new cluster-stop behavior is only partially visible in the patch excerpt, which is truncated. Its control flow (who may issue a stop, how the stops counter is authenticated between the two Macs, and how an older build treats a nil count) is outside the supplied evidence. This is a documentation change, but the described cluster control protocol could create a new attack surface for an unauthenticated peer to stop a pair, or for a replayed status reply to do so. I could not verify that from the supplied evidence. The next pass should check the implementing code for the ClusterControlReply authentication and the stop authorization, if that code is in the PR. Nothing here is flagged as a finding.
